title: Reachable End
statement:
Decide whether a hopper standing on the first cell can reach the last cell.

Contract
- `jumps` is a non-null, non-empty array of non-negative `int`s. A hopper starts at index `0`. From index `i` it may move forward to any index from `i + 1` up to `i + jumps[i]` (and not past the last index).
- Return `true` if the last index can be reached, otherwise `false`. A one-element array is already at its end.
- Values can be as large as `Integer.MAX_VALUE`; do not let `i + jumps[i]` overflow. Do not mutate `jumps`.

Examples
- `canReach(new int[]{2, 3, 1, 1, 4})` returns `true`.
- `canReach(new int[]{3, 2, 1, 0, 4})` returns `false`.
- `canReach(new int[]{0})` returns `true`.
hints: A zero in the array is not automatically a dead end: an earlier cell may jump over it.
Track the furthest index reachable so far while scanning left to right; if the scan reaches an index beyond that frontier, you are stuck.
One left-to-right pass with a single `long` (or overflow-safe) frontier is enough. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the array length.
inputSyntax: Input: the jump lengths in brackets or separated by spaces, for example: [2, 3, 1, 1, 4]
